nodes.label: desktop memory - where per-item AI cost exists at all

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. User principle, 2026-06-12: 'the cost for each extracted thing if using ai, matters. if it's just deterministic data extraction it's one thing, but as soon as it has to be interpreted or embedded, it matters.' The v2 pipeline's deterministic prefix - scan, probe, reference, structure, hard fields, chunking - can produce unlimited items at zero marginal cost, and the metered operations are exactly two: one tagger LLM call per chunk, and one embedding per phrase tag. Never propose embedding or LLM-interpreting data that is already exact; budget knobs live in the tagger contract, where chunk count is LLM calls and tags-per-chunk is embeddings, so a sane tag count per chunk is a cost decision and not only a quality one; and nodes-versus-attributes questions on the deterministic side are graph-hygiene questions, not cost questions. Distinct from no-cost-estimates, which bans cost framings at the user - this is a design principle about where per-item cost exists at all
